items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the composition of the state
board of parole and parole hearing officers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S289

SPONSOR: MYRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the composition of the
state board of parole and parole hearing officers

 
PURPOSE:

To make the composition of the parole board and parole hearing officers
geographically representative of the state's prison population.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill adds subdivision 2-a to § 259-b of the executive
law which requires that members of the parole board appointed or reap-
pointed on and after the effective date of this subdivision be so
constituted that the proportion of the members residing in any county of
the state shall be reasonably equivalent and in the same proportion as
the resident county of the inmate population bears to the total popu-
lation of the state.

Section two of the bill adds subdivision 3 to § 259-d of the executive
law which requires that hearing officers appointed or reappointed on and
after the effective date of this subdivision be so constituted that the
proportion of the members residing in any county of the state shall be
reasonably equivalent and in the same proportion as the resident county
of the inmate population bears to the total population of the state.

Section three of the bill provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

More than 75% of the New York State's prison population originates from
major urban areas of the state. When released, a majority will return to
their county of origin. Therefore, those who are instrumental in deter-
mining parole should understand and identify with the particular
concerns of the inmate's community or origin and return.This bill would
require members of the board of parole and parole hearing officers to be
representative of the county that the inmate population bears to the
total population of the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

summary: Requires the membership of the state board of parole, and parole hearing officers to be composed of a proportionate share of residents of each county to reflect the state's inmate population.
